$comment: Tier 2 writing styles for the restyle_draft MCP tool and the /restyle slash command. These are instructions for a language model, not deterministic rules — nothing here ever runs on cron, on save, or on pre-commit, and restyling always writes to a .draft.md sibling rather than the source.
$comment_constraints: Applied to every style. These exist because a rewrite that breaks the document is worse than no rewrite.
constraints: Never change the meaning of a technical statement — commands, flags, paths, versions, and API names are facts, not prose.
Never alter code blocks, inline code, URLs, file paths, frontmatter, or link targets.
Preserve the heading hierarchy and the order of sections.
Preserve every table's columns and rows; only cell prose may change.
Keep the document's language — do not translate as a side effect of restyling.
Obey the DVW markdown rules: single-asterisk italics, ISO dates, approved emoji only, no block elements inside list items.

casual.label: Casual
casual.instruction: Write as a colleague explaining to a colleague. Contractions are fine. Short sentences. Say what happened and why it matters. No corporate throat-clearing.

marketing.label: Marketing
marketing.instruction: Lead with the benefit, not the mechanism. Concrete over abstract. Active voice. Cut hedges and qualifiers. Never invent capabilities the source does not claim.

didactic.label: Didactic
didactic.instruction: Explain the why before the how. Introduce one idea per paragraph. Define a term the first time it appears. Prefer a worked example to an abstract description.

tutorial.label: Tutorial
tutorial.instruction: Numbered steps, one action per step, written in the imperative. State the expected result after each step so the reader can tell whether it worked. Put prerequisites at the top.

short.label: Short
short.instruction: Cut to roughly half the length without losing a fact. Remove restatement, throat-clearing, and transitional filler. Keep every number, name, and command.

series.label: Series
series.instruction: Write as one instalment of a sequence. Open by situating this part relative to the last, close by pointing at the next. Keep terminology identical across parts.

expert.label: Expert
expert.instruction: Assume domain fluency. Drop basic definitions and analogies. Use precise technical vocabulary. Lead with the non-obvious; state the interesting constraint first.

newbie.label: Newbie
newbie.instruction: Assume no prior knowledge. Expand every acronym on first use. Explain why a step exists, not only what it is. Flag the mistakes a newcomer is likely to make.

$comment_humour: Opt-in and never a default. Excluded from reference, API, and security documentation regardless of the flag.

light.instruction: At most one dry aside per major section, and only where it genuinely lands. Never at the reader's expense, never in a warning or an error-handling passage, never a joke that a non-native reader would have to decode. If nothing is funny, write it straight — forced humour reads worse than none.
